transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doc. Yeah, so, I’m here because... well, it’s kind of a lot, to be honest. I’m a firefighter, right? Which you’d think is the perfect job for a guy who likes to be on the go. And I do, I really do. But lately, it’s like... I just feel like I’m always running hot. Like, physically and mentally, just running at maximum capacity all the time. It’s like I have this engine inside me and I just can’t shut the motor off, no matter what I do or how exhausted I should be. 

Even when we’re back at the station and it’s supposed to be downtime, you know, when the other guys are just kicking back in the recliners, watching TV or trying to catch some sleep between calls, I just can't do it. I’m pacing the bays, or finding equipment to reorganize that doesn't need reorganizing, or just talking everyone’s ear off when they're trying to rest. And, well, that’s the main reason I finally made this appointment, because lately, that exact thing has been getting me in real trouble at the firehouse. My captain actually pulled me aside—I think it was Tuesday after a 24-hour shift—and he basically told me I'm driving the rest of the crew crazy and I need to get a handle on it. I just can't seem to power down, ever, and it's starting to mess with my job.
Have you also been feeling unusually euphoric or overly high in your mood, not just restless or on edge?

Euphoric? Like... really happy or on top of the world? No, no, definitely not that. I mean, don't get me wrong, sometimes you get that rush, right? Like if we have a really intense call, maybe a structure fire or a bad MVA—motor vehicle accident, you know—and everyone does their job perfectly and everyone goes home safe, sure, you feel great for a bit. You get that massive adrenaline dump. But that’s just normal job stuff, and it fades. 

What I’m dealing with on a daily basis, especially when we're just sitting around the station... it’s not a happy feeling at all. I'm not walking around feeling like Superman or like I'm in some unusually fantastic mood. It's actually incredibly frustrating. It's more like... well, it's exactly what you said, just restless. Edgy. Like I drank three entire pots of terrible, sludgy firehouse coffee and now my skin is vibrating, but there's absolutely no payoff to it. It’s not a good, high mood. If anything, I'm probably way more irritable than usual because I'm so annoyed that I can't just sit in the damn recliner and watch a movie for twenty minutes like a normal person. I just want to relax, and my brain is screaming at me to get up and move. So yeah, no, definitely not euphoric. Just... wired. Constantly, annoyingly wired.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still felt energized?

Less sleep? Man, I wish. I mean, no, no, not at all. I definitely don't feel energized. It's actually the exact opposite, which is probably the most frustrating part of this whole thing. 

Because, you know, with the schedule we work—we do 24 on, 48 off, or sometimes you get mandated for a 48-hour shift if a guy calls out sick or is on vacation—sleep is already this precious, unpredictable commodity. You never know when the tones are gonna drop. It could be 2 AM for an elderly lift assist, or 4 AM for a dumpster fire, or you might be up all night at a multi-alarm blaze. So when you actually get a chance to sleep at the station, you're supposed to take it. And my body? My body is exhausted. I'm 37, carrying 70 pounds of turnout gear and air packs... I feel it in my knees, my lower back. I *want* to sleep. I know I desperately *need* the sleep. 

But then I go into the bunk room, and it's like... I just lie there. I'm staring at the ceiling tiles, listening to the other guys snore, and my brain is just going and going and going. I'll be tossing and turning, thinking about, I don't know, fixing the busted latch on the compartment door on Engine 4, or realizing we need to restock the 4x4 gauze in the medical jump bag, or just completely random stuff that doesn't matter at all at three in the morning. I'm dead on my feet, completely drained, but I can't actually cross that bridge into falling asleep because I'm so keyed up. 

It’s like... it's like your phone battery is at one percent, right? But the screen brightness is stuck on maximum and the flashlight won't turn off, and you can't plug it in. So, no, I definitely don't feel energized on less sleep. I feel totally wiped out. I just feel exhausted and wired at the exact same time, which is why I end up just getting out of bed and pacing the apparatus floor until the sun comes up.
Were you like this as a kid too—especially having trouble paying attention in school?

Yeah, actually. It's funny you bring that up, because I was just talking to my mom about this whole situation with my captain, and she basically just laughed and said, "Welcome to my world." She says I was exactly like this back in grade school, too. 

I mean, if you ask her, she’ll tell you I was an absolute nightmare for my teachers. I literally could not stay in my seat. You know those old school desks, the ones where the chair is connected to the desk part with that metal bar? I was always tipping them back, or I'd just stand up in the middle of a math lesson to go look out the window or sharpen my pencil for the fifth time that hour. I just had to be moving. And the blurting... man, I'd just blurt answers out all the time. The teacher would ask a question to the class, and before she even finished the sentence, the answer would just shoot out of my mouth. I wouldn't raise my hand, I wouldn't wait to be called on, it was just like this reflex I couldn't control. I wasn't trying to be a bad kid or disrespectful, I just couldn't hold it in.

And the disorganization was just off the charts. My backpack was like a black hole. I was constantly losing my homework. The frustrating part was that half the time I’d actually sit at the kitchen table and do the worksheet, but then it would end up crumpled into a ball at the bottom of my bag under a pair of dirty gym socks, or I'd just leave it on the counter at home. So my mom was always getting notes sent home. Like, constantly. Those little handwritten notes from the teacher stapled to my agenda, or phone calls saying I was being disruptive or missing assignments again. 

Which is the crazy part, because my mom always makes a point to say that I was bright enough to do the work. The teachers would even write that in the notes! They'd say, "He's very smart, he catches on quickly, but he just won't apply himself." Like, I understood the material perfectly fine. If you asked me a question, I knew the answer—obviously, since I was shouting it across the room—but I just could not do the actual sitting still, focusing, and turning-in-the-paperwork part of school. So yeah, I guess it’s definitely not a new thing, it’s just... it's following me around, you know? Just playing out differently now that I'm an adult trying to keep my career from going off the rails.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energetic or high and needed much less sleep than usual?

Several days? Like, a stretch of three or four days feeling energetic on no sleep? No, no way. Like I was saying just a minute ago, it's really the exact opposite. If I go a couple of days without sleep—which, you know, happens in this line of work, like if we get a major incident, a multi-alarm fire or something where everyone gets called in and you're just working on adrenaline and protein bars for 48 hours—I am absolutely wrecked by the end of it. I mean, my body feels like it's been run over by a ladder truck. 

There was this one time last summer, we had this massive brush fire out on the county line, and the wind kept shifting, so we were out there cutting line and hauling hoses for almost three days straight. And yeah, while you're in it, you're moving, you're doing the job, but it's not some... unusually high feeling. It's just pure survival mode. And the second we got back to the bay and peeled our gear off, I was a total zombie. I crashed so hard. 

So, if you mean just sitting around in normal life, off-duty, and suddenly I go on some three-day stretch of feeling fantastic and not needing to sleep? Never. Never happens. If I'm not sleeping, it's because my brain won't shut up and let me rest, like I mentioned, but I feel every single second of that exhaustion. My eyes burn, I get this dull headache right behind my temples, my knees ache... I feel it all. I want the sleep so bad. I'm definitely not walking around feeling energized or high, I'm just dragging myself through the day feeling completely drained but still somehow unable to just sit still. So, no, definitely no periods of feeling like that for days on end. I wish I had that kind of energy, honestly, but no.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder with clear childhood onset, persistent hyperactivity/impulsivity, and current adult impairment at work. He reported longstanding inability to stay seated, excessive fidgeting/pacing, blurting out answers, disorganization, and difficulty sustaining attention/turning in assignments since grade school, with ongoing occupational disruption as a firefighter. He denied euphoric mood, decreased need for sleep, or multi-day episodes of elevated energy, making a bipolar-spectrum diagnosis unlikely.
